summary:
Oyo stands under Nigeria's national framework, including the Same-Sex Marriage (Prohibition) Act 2014, which applies in the state as it does elsewhere in the country.

Oyo is a southern state outside the Shari'a regime. The death-penalty exposure for male same-sex conduct that applies in twelve northern states does not reach Oyo. The criminal code in force in the state is the Criminal Code, which criminalises sex between men with up to 14 years' imprisonment and gross indecency with up to 3 years.

No anti-discrimination protection exists for LGBTI people in Oyo.

Dating applications carry an entrapment risk that is not confined to any one city. Criminal gangs pose as potential dates on popular apps, lure men to meetings, film them and then extort, beat or kidnap them; one investigative report interviewed 21 people about being targeted this way. The documented cases and the underground scene described are based in Lagos, and the sources extend the same risk to gay and transgender app users in Oyo. Victims seldom report to the police, because making a report carries its own risk of arrest or assault.
tangentialFactors:
Oyo's exposure sits below the northern Shari'a states. Twelve states in the north of the country apply Shari'a law under which male same-sex conduct carries a maximum of death, and Oyo is not one of them. The maximum a visitor faces in Oyo is the 14 years available under the Criminal Code and the national statute.

Enforcement of the national statute has been documented mainly as mass arrests at parties and social venues and as police profiling and extortion of people perceived as gay. No operation of that kind in Oyo appears in the sources, so the state's own enforcement record is not separately visible.
localsOnly:
The Criminal Code offences in force in Oyo apply to residents as well as to visitors, and no anti-discrimination protection exists for LGBTI residents in employment, housing or services.

No Oyo-based LGBTI organisation, health service or support network is documented in the sources, and no state-level body addressing the safety of LGBTI residents appears in them.
outOfScopeNotes:
No arrest, prosecution or violent incident in Oyo is documented in the sources. The national enforcement record is not disaggregated by state, so the frequency of enforcement in Oyo cannot be stated.

The dating-application extortion cases documented by the investigative reporting are based in Lagos; the sources extend the risk to app users in Oyo without recording an Oyo case.

Whether the Criminal Code offences in Oyo are applied to transgender and gender-nonconforming people specifically, as distinct from gay men, is not documented in the sources.
